title: Bend a 45 degree offset in 3/8 in tube on a hand tube bender
instruction: Bend the tube into a 45 degree offset with parallel ends at its two yellow bands, lay it on the green template, and move both hands away.
context: Plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters (O*NET 47-2152.00, 510,600 US workers) and heating, air conditioning and refrigeration mechanics (49-9021.00, 397,450; "bend pipe or tubing") bend offsets in tube by hand to step a run round an obstruction. Swagelok's hand tube bender manual gives the layout: the bend marks lie O x 1.414 apart for a 45 degree offset (MS-13-43, p.11). Two opposite bends at two measured marks, the tube re-fed and turned over between them, ends left parallel at a set offset: the result to measure is the offset and the parallel ends, not one angle. A bend can't be undone and each springs back.
setup: A hand tube bender of the class of the Swagelok MS-HTB-6T (3/8 in tube, 15/16 in = 23.8 mm bend radius) on the table; this model matches its bend radius only, see fidelity. A white low-friction bed 42 x 74 cm, 4 mm thick, covers x 4 to 46 cm and y -22 to 52 cm. On it stands a steel former, 4.8 cm across (2.4 cm radius) and 5 cm tall, with its axis at (24, -8) cm and a red mark on top pointing to the bending point at (29, -8) cm. A guide of two steel rails 8 cm long, 1 cm wide and 1.8 cm tall runs along y from -11 to -19 cm, with 3 cm between them, centred on x = 29 cm. A blue aluminium handle turns about the former's axis, 15 cm long, its beam 7.5 to 8.5 cm above the bed, starting along +x and turning anticlockwise from above to a stop at 145 degrees. A steel shoe 1.6 cm square hangs from it 8 cm from the axis. A red sleeve knob 3.6 cm square, free to turn, tops its end, reaching 11.5 cm above the bed. The tube is real 3/8 in (9.5 mm) round, but drawn and modelled as a steel bar 2 cm square, so that it reads from above: 35 cm long, 195 g, with two yellow bands 3 cm long and 14.0 cm apart (9.9 cm x 1.414), centred on its length. An orange aluminium grip block 2 x 4 x 4 cm, 86 g, sits on top midway between the bands. It lies straight along x with the block at (26, 40) cm. Two green lanes 4 x 12.5 cm are painted on the bed, centred at (23.7, 11.8) cm and (13.8, 32.2) cm. Positions are from the arm bases' midpoint in x and the table's centre line in y, with +y toward the left arm. The screenshot shows the start.
scoring: Read at the end of the run. A hand is a gripper's fingertip midpoint, and the tube counts as let go only with both hands 6 cm or more from each of its three straight parts. A band starts bending only within 1.2 cm of the bending point in x and y, with the part on its -y side within 10 degrees of the y axis, and it bends only while the handle is advancing and its shoe is pressing the tube: a hand can't bend it. Each bend springs back 3 degrees when the shoe comes off. A band that has reached 48 degrees before springback locks for good then; one short of that can take another sweep. 0 for good if a bend passes 55 degrees, if the two bends go the same way so the ends aren't an offset, or if any part of the tube leaves the bed. 0 if it isn't let go, or if no bend reaches 45 degrees +/- 6. Otherwise 0.25 for one bend at 45 +/- 6 degrees, in either order; 0.5 for both; 0.75 with the two ends parallel within 5 degrees and 9.9 +/- 1 cm apart; 0.9 with it also on the template, each straight end's middle within 1.5 cm across and 2.5 cm along a lane's centre and within 8 degrees of the lane, either way round; 1.0 with it also at rest (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for the last 1 s. The 9.9 cm offset follows from the formula; all the tolerances are this task's own, not a maker's or an industry limit.
reset_notes: A bent tube can't be straightened, so a real trial takes a fresh length. Set the handle back along +x and the fresh tube straight on the bed as in the screenshot. On real tube, mark each bend 360 degrees round, 14.0 cm apart, and a direction mark on the outside of each bend.
fidelity: Rigid parts, not a material: the tube is three 2 cm square steel parts on two one-way hinges (real: 3/8 in round tube), drawn thicker so it reads from above. A bend's set angle follows the handle by rule; springback is a set 3 degrees. No bend radius or bend force is modelled. The bender has a fixed former and one 15 cm handle; the real tool has roll dies, a tube latch and two longer handles. The grip block is added.
